home-lgu-cta-subtitle: Birth certificates, business permits and barangay concerns go to your city or municipal hall. The Province runs provincial hospitals, roads, social welfare and more. Find the right office first.
home-map-description: Interactive map of the Province of Bukidnon in Northern Mindanao. The marker shows the Provincial Capitol in Malaybalay City, at about 8.1575°N, 125.1278°E.
home-history-precolonial: The highlands are home to the Bukidnon, Higaonon, Talaandig, Manobo, Matigsalug, Tigwahanon and Umayamnon peoples, the seven tribes of Bukidnon.
home-history-1850s: Under Spanish rule, the area becomes part of the province of Misamis.
home-history-1907: Act No. 1693 creates the province of Agusan with Bukidnon as a sub-province. Malaybalay becomes its capital.
home-history-1917: Act No. 2711 makes Bukidnon a regular province on 10 March, now celebrated as the province's founding anniversary.
home-history-1977: The provincial government holds the first organized Kaamulan Festival, a gathering of the seven tribes.
home-history-cityhood: Malaybalay becomes a city in 1998 (Republic Act No. 8490), followed by Valencia in 2001.
home-history-2012: Republic Act No. 10184 divides Bukidnon into four congressional districts, in effect from the 2013 elections.
home-history-card-tribes: Kaamulan comes from the Binukid word "amul", to gather. The festival brings the seven tribes to Malaybalay around the 10 March founding anniversary.
home-history-card-highlands: Mount Dulang-dulang in the Kitanglad Range, about 2,938 meters high, is the second highest peak in the Philippines. Bukidnon's plateau farms earn it the name "food basket of Mindanao".
